Haar.et:
From Middle High German and Old High German hār, from Proto-West Germanic *hār, from Proto-Germanic *hērą, from Proto-Indo-European *keres- (“rough hair, bristle”).
Compare Dutch haar, West Frisian hier, English hair, Danish hår.

s: a municipality of Lower Austria, Austria
hair's breadth; whisker (very small distance between two things)
Es hat nur eine Haaresbreite gefehlt und ich wäre vom LKW überfahren worden.
Haaresbreite.et: From Haar (“hair”) + -es- + Breite (“breadth”), literally “breadth of a hair”.

s: hairpiece (tuft of false hair used to make one's hair look more luxuriant)
